content: Serine/threonine-protein kinase SMG1 is an enzyme encoded by the SMG1 gene in humans. This enzyme is a member of the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase-related kinase (PIKK) protein family. The SMG1 gene encodes a protein that plays a critical role in the process of nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD), which is a cellular mechanism responsible for the surveillance and degradation of mRNA transcripts containing premature stop codons. This protein exhibits kinase activity and is believed to contribute to NMD by phosphorylating the protein known as regulator of nonsense transcripts 1 (UPF1). Although alternative splicing of SMG1 transcripts has been reported, the complete sequences and functional implications of these variants remain undetermined. The SMG1 protein has been demonstrated to interact with protein kinase C iota (PRKCI) and UPF1, highlighting its involvement in complex molecular pathways.
